records.text: Lanie Reed is a gryphon master who arranges gryphon travel. She is openly wary of the Dark Iron, including those affiliated with the Thorium Brotherhood, and threatens to meet any who approach her with her mattock.
Grisha is a wind rider master who arranges travel by wind rider. He says there will be no trouble while the nearby dwarves stay away and asks travelers where they are headed.
Margol the Rager is a named beast combatant in Searing Gorge who uses combat abilities during fights.
These enslaved workers fear discovery by their captors and warn strangers to leave before the slavers notice. Some ask whether the visitor has come to rescue them.
Dark Iron slavers operate in the Searing Gorge and use nets in combat. Taskmaster Scrange marks them and the Dark Iron taskmasters as competition to be culled.
Dark Iron taskmasters use Battle Command in combat. Taskmaster Scrange singles them out as competition to be culled in the Searing Gorge.
Blazing elementals are fiery elemental beings.
Inferno elementals are fiery elemental beings.
Tempered war golems are elemental constructs with a military role.
Twilight Dark Shamans are humanoids found in Searing Gorge. A Symbol of Ragnaros can be recovered from one; Kalaran Windblade seeks such a symbol to try to form a magical torch casing.
A Twilight Fire Guard is a fire-themed member of the Twilight's Hammer forces in Searing Gorge, serving as a guard among the cult's humanoid ranks.
A Twilight Geomancer is a geomancy-themed member of the Twilight's Hammer forces in Searing Gorge, part of the cult's humanoid ranks.
Sarah Tanner is an Elemental Leatherworking trainer in Searing Gorge. She offers training and a path to unlearn the specialization.
Rekk'tilac is a beast found in Searing Gorge.
Smoldar is a named elite elemental in Searing Gorge. Its combat behavior includes casting a spell when engaged.
A Faulty War Golem is an elite construct in Searing Gorge. Its combat behavior includes casting a spell when wounded.
Shleipnarr is a demon.
Scald is an elemental being.
Highlord Mastrogonde is a highlord found in Searing Gorge.
Blackheart is a slave overseer.

Dorius Stonetender is an injured dwarf seeking help to return to Ironforge. Dorius insists that the Cauldron's location be remembered, fearing the team will remain trapped in its mine if anything happens to their guide. Short of breath during the escape, Dorius complains of needing rest and wanting to quit smoking.

Obsidion is a named creation that the enslaved archaeologists were made to complete. It begins as an unattackable object, then becomes a hostile target to be slain; its heart is taken as proof of its defeat.
An enslaved archaeologist in the Searing Gorge workings, part of the population held by the Dark Irons and forced to work in the Slag Pits.

A dying archaeologist in Dorius's excavation unit asks that the other enslaved workers be freed. He directs the listener to retrieve a Twilight's Hammer relic and place it on the Altar of Suntara, then collapses.
A Twilight's Hammer idolater who treats intruders as infidels and calls for their execution or sacrifice to Ragnaros. The cultist is encountered at prayer and fights with fire magic.

Zamael Lunthistle speaks from a cage of a faith rekindled after years of malevolent deeds against the world and its inhabitants. He says he does not expect absolution, but asks that his prayer to Elune, etched on a golden tablet, be recovered and taken to Astarii Starseeker in Darnassus. He accepts his fate in the cage, yet insists the prayer must be found.

Nilith Lokrav is concerned that poachers are killing Searing Gorge spiders carelessly, threatening a valued source of shadow silk. She wants the poachers stopped and points to Raze as a source of help. She also targets the Undermarket operation led by Trade Master Kovic, citing its Dark Iron ties; after Kovic's defeat, she wants Vizzklick in Gadgetzan told, expecting him to welcome the news.

Raze is Nilith's guardian in the Searing Gorge, a powerful, simple-spoken protector who offers to smash the Shadowsilk Poachers when directed. He can follow and attack them at a player's signal; his dialogue calls the signal a stick. He speaks of himself in the third person and says when he is going home.
A Shadowsilk Poacher of the Undermarket in the Searing Gorge, part of a group that slaughters local spiders for their valuable shadow silk. Raze can be directed to attack the poachers.

Trade Master Kovic heads the Undermarket operation in the Searing Gorge and has close ties with the region's Dark Iron dwarves. Nilith describes the Undermarket as cutthroat traders willing to do almost anything for the right price, and identifies Kovic as the target of a strike against its leadership.
Clunk is identified by Nilith as Trade Master Kovic's minion and a member of the Undermarket operation in the Searing Gorge. Nilith names Clunk as a target alongside Kovic.

Kalaran Windblade is driven by vengeance and plans to strike the defenses at four sentry towers. He has you gather elemental materials and a Twilight’s Hammer symbol to make and enchant the Torch of Retribution, then directs you to set the towers ablaze. His dry, mocking humor contrasts with the serious aim of disrupting their guard posts.

Squire Maltrake is Kalaran Windblade’s envoy and instructs you in using the Torch of Retribution against the four sentry towers. He addresses Kalaran as “master,” says he lives only to serve him, and greets the towers’ fires with eager praise. He also warns you about the Dark Iron lookouts posted there.
A Dark Iron lookout posted at the sentry towers, this armed watcher shoots at attackers and may flee for help when badly wounded.
Dark Iron Watchmen stand as armed sentries in the local Dark Iron presence. This watchman answers threats with a direct strike, a plain expression of its guard role.
Muck Splash is an elemental creature found in this part of the region.
Incendosaurs inhabit the lava pools of the Slag Pit in the Cauldron and are considered a hazard to exploration there.
A Fire Beetle is a tiny critter, found across several regions.
Graw Cornerstone sells mail armor and repairs equipment.

Overseer Maltorius is a Dark Iron commander in the Slag Pit, formerly a Thorium Brotherhood agent. Brotherhood accounts accuse him of leaving the clan with its fiery flux recipe and describe him as a traitor.
A sentry of the Thorium Brotherhood, keeping watch on behalf of the organization.

Master Smith Burninate directs fiery flux work for the Thorium Brotherhood in Searing Gorge. He calls Maltorius a traitor for taking the clan's recipe and wants the secret plans recovered. He presses helpers to replenish the dwindling supply, impatiently urging them to hurry if they want acceptance in the Brotherhood.

Overseer Oilfist is a Thorium Brotherhood official at Thorium Point in Searing Gorge. He describes his remit as the Brotherhood's mining, smithing and guard duties, and says recent necessity has pushed it toward a more martial role. When presented with a colossus chitin sample, he praises its potential for powerful armor.

Taskmaster Scrange is a Thorium Brotherhood taskmaster at the Searing Gorge compound, with a wry, deliberately bureaucratic sense of humor. He describes making every kind of business tedious, while his work includes recruiting help against Dark Iron rivals and seeking stolen tools for the Brotherhood.

Hansel Heavyhands is a Thorium Brotherhood dwarf whose complaints about swollen fingers, bunions, and the cold give his orders a comic, weary edge. He delegates dangerous work around the Gorge, explaining that Scrange and Burninate assigned him the Incendosaur problem so expedition teams can explore the Slag Pit. He says Lolo calls on him to mete out justice and pain.

Evonice Sootsmoker is a Thorium Brotherhood member in the Searing Gorge. She targets the Dark Iron workforce with pillow thefts, reasoning that deprived dwarves will lose rest and productivity. Her delight at acquiring Chambermaid Pillaclencher’s ornate magical pillow, and her boast that she is the smart one despite her “crazy goggles,” give her a sly, self-assured edge.

Lookout Captain Lolo Longstriker serves the Thorium Brotherhood in the Searing Gorge and receives the bounty on Overseer Maltorius. Lolo describes themself as blind and credits drink with keeping their senses sharp; their slurred, joking response to Maltorius’s severed head carries the same irreverent humor.

Elder Ironband is a named elder associated with the old races and the New Year observance. In a greeting, Ironband speaks of the new year and bright moon as the time when “the ancients awake.” The elder’s greeting to visitors who pay homage is gracious and offers a token.
Metzen is a named reindeer belonging to Smokywood Pastures and one of Greatfather Winter’s reindeer. During Winter Veil, kidnappers hold him, and adventurers are asked to find and free him.

A Dark Iron kidnapper guarding Winter Veil plunder, including the stolen reindeer. When intruders arrive, the bandit rallies others against the rescuers and taunts them with pirate-like threats, invoking Greatfather Winter and the holiday.

place_records.text: You are in Searing Gorge in the Eastern Kingdoms, land held by neither the Alliance nor the Horde. Its main settlement is Thorium Point. Dark Iron dwarves hold the Slag Pit and keep enslaved workers there, and the region is troubled by Dark Iron taskmasters, spiders, war golems and incendosaurs.

You are in The Cauldron, an area of Searing Gorge where Dark Iron slavers and taskmasters keep enslaved workers. The workers warn strangers to leave before the slavers notice, and some ask whether the visitor has come to rescue them. A spirit healer here offers a return to life for a price, though the healer cautions that the traveler's time may not yet have come. Magma elementals and heavy war golems roam the area.

You are in Grimesilt Dig Site, a dig in Searing Gorge. Dark Iron geologists and watchmen, tempered war golems and glassweb spiders trouble the site. Dorius Stonetender, an Alliance dwarf, is badly hurt and wants to get back to Ironforge, and Dorius insists that the location of the Cauldron be remembered.

You are in Firewatch Ridge, part of Searing Gorge held by Twilight cultists. Zamael Lunthistle, an Alliance captive, speaks from a cage. He says his faith was rekindled after years of malevolent deeds and that he does not expect absolution, and he asks that his prayer to Elune, etched on a golden tablet, be recovered. Twilight fire guards, geomancers and idolaters are the dangers here.
You are in The Sea of Cinders, a part of Searing Gorge where searing lava spiders are the main danger. Magma elementals and blazing elementals also roam it, and Dark Iron lookouts watch the area.

You are in Blackrock Mountain, part of Searing Gorge. Anvilrage enforcers and taskmasters and magma elementals are the dangers here. Quarry slaves are among the humanoid workers found in the region, and they strike directly when attacked.

You are in Thorium Point, the main settlement of Searing Gorge, which is held by neither side. Lanie Reed, a gryphon master, serves the Alliance here, and Grisha, a wind rider master, serves the Horde. The Thorium Brotherhood keeps a compound under Master Smith Burninate, and Lanie Reed is wary of the Dark Iron. Dark Iron taskmasters, slavers and greater lava spiders trouble the ground around it.
You are in Blackchar Cave, a cave in Searing Gorge. Anvilrage enforcers and taskmasters and greater lava spiders are its main dangers, and Overmaster Pyron is a notable one.

You are in Tanner Camp, a camp in Searing Gorge. Sarah Tanner, an Alliance leatherworker, teaches Elemental Leatherworking here and also knows how to undo that specialization. Glassweb spiders and a rekk'tilac roam nearby.
You are in Dustfire Valley, a valley in Searing Gorge where glassweb spiders, Dark Iron geologists and tempered war golems are the dangers.

You are in The Slag Pit, a Dark Iron workings in Searing Gorge. Dark Iron taskmasters keep enslaved archaeologists at work here, and Incendosaurs, Slave Master Blackheart and Obsidion haunt the pits. The enslaved workers fear discovery and warn strangers to leave, though some ask whether a visitor has come to free them. A dying archaeologist asks that the others be freed.
